messages:
viv: Quick decision for the 3-day mini: two competing follow-up asks after launch — (A) urgent embeddings pipeline regression affecting search quality for a subset of enterprise customers, or (B) ship a batching+cache change that could cut embedding unit costs ~12% but requires infra work. Which do we pick?

enrique: Cost wins in the medium-term but regression is causing noisy CS tickets and a drop in query CTR. We have 4 escalations flagged.

sam: +1 for regression. We can't let search relevance degrade for paid tenants. If it's a small revert or focused guard we can ship quickly.

tara: Heads-up on test infra: embedding e2e is flaky so add a buffer. If we pick regression, scope it to a targeted fix + tests that catch the malformed vector path.

enrique: The batching+cache work requires touched pieces in serving runtime and routing. I'd budget 3 dev days and an ops window for rollout. Risk: cache cold-start could spike p99s if not carefully shaded.

viv: Can we do both in a split approach? Regression first, and prep the batching change as a flag-off PR so it's ready for Wave B? That keeps momentum on cost work but doesn't block the mini.

sam: That seems reasonable. Proposed plan: 1) regression: triage + failing test today, minimal patch (parse guard + fallback) + canary to 5%; 2) batching: Enrique to draft RFC + flag-off PR with perf harness and safety guard so it can be picked up next week.

tara: I'll own the regression integration test and add a flakiness buffer of +0.5 days. Also will add an explicit acceptance test that reproduces the customer payload.

enrique: I'll start the batching RFC and create a ticket "prepped: batching-cache (flag-off)" with ACs and perf harness notes. Will list the safety gates (cache TTL, warmup strategy, backpressure).

sam: For regression PR, I'll open branch hotfix/embed-parse-guard and add a WIP PR with failing unit + integration tests. Local repro snippet for devs: 

```
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV' -d '{"input":"\u0000weird\u0000payload"}'
```

viv: Ops ask: can we set a canary SLI watch for embed_relevance_score_drop and embed_error_rate? Also surface the batching experiment cohort separately when it exists.

ops-bot: Canary dashboard card created: "canary/embed-regression-2199998888". Alerts set: embed_error_rate > 0.5% or embed_relevance_delta < -0.02.

sam: I'll push WIP PR today and assign @tara for tests and @enrique for context. Target: canary within 24h of merge.

enrique: I'll create the flag-off PR for batching/caching and include a small perf harness script so we can baseline quickly. Tagging it as "wave-b: ready".

tara: Customer comms: I'll draft a short note for affected tenants after canary is green. Keep it brief: what we changed + expected restore of relevance + contact.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for commit b7c2d9 to cluster shore-1.

viv: Recap of action items: Sam -> PR + minimal patch; Tara -> integration tests + flakiness buffer; Enrique -> batching RFC + flag-off PR + perf harness; Ops -> canary watch; Viv -> update roadmap board and move batching work to Wave B prepped state. Target: canary verification within 24h. Any objections?

enrique: No objections.

sam: No objections, starting the patch now.

tara: Ack, will pair on the integration test tomorrow AM.

ops-bot: Monitoring enabled for canary/embed-regression-2199998888.

viv: Thanks team. We'll follow up in #postlaunch for status and I'll ping stakeholders once canary is green. :thumbsup:
